questions.question:
From medial to lateral, what is the correct anatomical sequence of the deep contents located
within the cubital fossa?
options: Radial nerve → Biceps tendon → Brachial artery → Median nerve
Median nerve → Brachial artery → Biceps brachii tendon → Radial nerve
Brachial artery → Median nerve → Biceps tendon → Radial nerve
Biceps tendon → Brachial artery → Median nerve → Ulnar nerve
questions.answer: Median nerve → Brachial artery → Biceps brachii tendon → Radial nerve
questions.explanation:
From  medial to lateral , the mnemonic  "MBBR"  (Median nerve, Brachial artery, Biceps tendon,
Radial nerve [deep between brachialis and brachioradialis]) outlines the contents. Clinically, the bicipital
aponeurosis separates these deep contents from the superficial median cubital vein, protecting the artery during
venipuncture.

BRACHIAL PLEXUS & NERVE INJURY

questions.question:
A 52-year-old painter reports severe pain when abducting the right arm, especially between 60°
and 120°. On examination, he is completely unable to initiate the first 15° of abduction. Which
muscle is most likely torn?
questions.explanation:
The  supraspinatus  muscle (innervated by the suprascapular nerve, C5–C6) initiates the first 0°–
15° of arm abduction at the glenohumeral joint. The deltoid muscle continues abduction from 15° to 90°, while
the trapezius and serratus anterior rotate the scapula upwards beyond 90°. Supraspinatus is the most
commonly torn rotator cuff tendon due to subacromial impingement.
 Clinical Anatomy: Upper Limb Question Bank  Page 1 of 7

HUMERUS FRACTURES & PERIPHERAL NERVES
 Q

questions.question:
A 24-year-old motorcyclist is thrown from his bike, landing violently on his shoulder while his
head is forced to the opposite side. Examination reveals an adducted, internally rotated arm
with an extended elbow and pronated forearm ("waiter's tip" posture). Which roots of the
brachial plexus are most likely injured?
questions.explanation:
This presentation describes  Erb-Duchenne palsy (Erb's palsy) , caused by traction or rupture of
the upper trunk (roots C5 and C6) due to an excessive increase in the angle between neck and shoulder.
Damage to the suprascapular, axillary, and musculocutaneous nerves paralyzes the abductors (deltoid,
supraspinatus), lateral rotators (infraspinatus, teres minor), elbow flexors (biceps, brachialis), and supinators
(biceps brachii), producing the classic "waiter's tip" limb posture.
 SHOULDER & ROTATOR CUFF
 Q

questions.question:
A mid-shaft fracture of the humerus is most likely to injure which nerve and associated blood
vessel located along the radial (spiral) groove?
options: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
Ulnar nerve and superior ulnar collateral artery
questions.answer: Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
questions.explanation:
The  radial nerve  and  profunda brachii artery  (deep artery of the arm) course together along the
spiral groove on the posterior surface of the humeral shaft. Mid-shaft fractures frequently lacerate or entrap the
radial nerve, leading to "wrist drop" (loss of wrist and finger extension) and sensory loss on the dorsum of the
first web space.
 WRIST & HAND ANATOMY
 Q

questions.question:
A 45-year-old computer programmer presents with nocturnal tingling, numbness, and burning
pain over the palmar aspect of the lateral three and a half digits. Thenar muscle wasting is
noted. Which structure is spared because its branch does not pass through the carpal tunnel?
options: Palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve
questions.answer: Palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve
questions.explanation:
In  carpal tunnel syndrome , structures traversing deep to the flexor retinaculum (median nerve, 4
FDS tendons, 4 FDP tendons, 1 FPL tendon) are compressed. However, the  palmar cutaneous branch  of the
median nerve branches off approximately 5 cm proximal to the flexor retinaculum and passes  superficial  to it,
preserving cutaneous sensation over the central palm.
 Clinical Anatomy: Upper Limb Question Bank  Page 2 of 7

CARPAL BONES & CLINICAL PATHOLOGY
 Q

questions.question:
Following a fall onto an outstretched hand (FOOSH), a 21-year-old athlete has tenderness in the
anatomical snuffbox. Radiographs confirm a fracture across the waist of the scaphoid. What is
the most significant clinical risk associated with this fracture?
options: Avascular necrosis of the proximal pole
questions.answer: Avascular necrosis of the proximal pole
questions.explanation:
The blood supply to the  scaphoid bone  is retrograde, entering primarily via distal branches of the
radial artery and flowing from distal to proximal. A fracture across the scaphoid waist interrupts blood flow to the
proximal segment, predisposing it to nonunion and  avascular necrosis (AVN) .
 ANATOMICAL SPACES
 Q

questions.question:
Which structure traverses the quadrangular space of the posterior scapular region alongside
the axillary nerve?
questions.explanation:
The  quadrangular space  is bounded superiorly by teres minor (or subscapularis), inferiorly by
teres major, medially by the long head of triceps brachii, and laterally by the surgical neck of the humerus. It
transmits the  axillary nerve  and  posterior circumflex humeral artery . Fractures of the surgical neck or
anterior shoulder dislocations can compromise both structures.
 CUBITAL FOSSA RELATIONS
 Q

questions.question:
A difficult breech delivery involving excessive upward traction on the upper limb damages the
lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8–T1). The infant demonstrates a "claw hand" posture and
ipsilateral Horner syndrome. What is this clinical condition called?
questions.explanation:
Klumpke palsy  results from lower trunk (C8–T1) brachial plexus injury, typically due to upward
pulling on an abducted arm (e.g., breech delivery or grabbing a tree branch while falling). It paralyzes intrinsic
hand muscles (lumbricals, interossei, thenar/hypothenar), producing a total claw hand. Concomitant injury to the
T1 sympathetic fibers leads to  Horner syndrome  (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis).
 AXILLA & CHEST WALL
 Q

questions.question:
During a radical mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, the long thoracic nerve of Bell
is accidentally severed. Which deformity will become apparent upon pushing forward against a
wall?
questions.explanation:
The  long thoracic nerve  (roots C5, C6, C7 — "C5, 6, 7 raise your arms to heaven") courses
along the superficial surface of the  serratus anterior  muscle. Denervation impairs scapular protraction and
upward rotation, causing the medial border and inferior angle of the scapula to project posteriorly ("winged
scapula"), especially when pushing against resistance.

questions.question:
Which pair of muscles is responsible for adducting the fingers toward the axial line of the hand
(third digit) and abducting them away from it, respectively?
options: Flexor digitorum profundus and Extensor digitorum
questions.explanation:
Remember the mnemonic  PAD & DAB :  P almar interossei  AD duct the digits toward the midline
(3rd digit), and  D orsal interossei  AB duct the digits away from the midline. All interossei are innervated by the
deep branch of the  ulnar nerve  (C8, T1).
 SURFACE ANATOMY & SPACES
 Q

questions.question:
Which tendon forms the medial boundary of the anatomical snuffbox when viewed in the
anatomical position?
questions.explanation:
The  anatomical snuffbox  is bounded medially (posteriorly) by the tendon of  extensor pollicis
longus (EPL) , which hooks around Lister's tubercle on the radius. The lateral (anterior) boundary is formed by
the tendons of  abductor pollicis longus (APL)  and  extensor pollicis brevis (EPB) . The floor contains the
scaphoid, trapezium, and the radial artery.
 ELBOW PATHOLOGY & NERVES
 Q

questions.question:
The pectoralis minor muscle divides the axillary artery into three anatomical parts. Which
branch arises from the second part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation:
The rule of branches per part of the axillary artery: Part 1 (proximal to pectoralis minor) has  1
branch : Superior thoracic artery.
Part 2 (deep to pectoralis minor) has  2 branches :  Thoracoacromial artery  and Lateral thoracic artery.
Part 3 (distal to pectoralis minor) has  3 branches : Subscapular artery, Anterior circumflex humeral artery, and
Posterior circumflex humeral artery.
 FOREARM & HAND INNERVATION
 Q

questions.question:
A patient is unable to make the "OK" sign; instead, when attempting to pinch index finger to
thumb, the distal phalanges remain flat in an abnormal pad-to-pad pinch. Which nerve is
compressed or damaged?
questions.explanation:
The  anterior interosseous nerve (AIN)  is a pure motor branch of the median nerve supplying 3
deep flexors:  flexor pollicis longus ,  lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus  (digits 2 and 3), and  pronator
quadratus . Inability to flex the DIP joint of the index finger and IP joint of the thumb produces a characteristic
pinch deformity rather than a circular "OK" gesture. No cutaneous sensory loss occurs.
 Clinical Anatomy: Upper Limb Question Bank  Page 6 of 7

JOINTS & LIGAMENTS
 Q

questions.question:
A 2-year-old child is lifted abruptly by the wrist by an older sibling. The child cries out and holds
the forearm pronated and slightly flexed, refusing to move it ("nursemaid's elbow"). Which
ligament has subluxated over the radial head?
questions.explanation:
In young children, the head of the radius is relatively small and cone-shaped. Sudden axial
traction on an extended, pronated forearm causes the radial head to slip out from the  annular ligament ,
becoming partially trapped between the radial head and the capitulum of the humerus. Gentle supination with
elbow flexion typically reduces the subluxation.
 Clinical Anatomy: Upper Limb Question Bank  Page 7 of 7

questions.question: A 45-year-old female presents with nocturnal paresthesia in the lateral three and a half digits. Physical exam reveals thenar wasting. Which anatomical structure is spared because its branch does NOT pass through the carpal tunnel?
options: Palmar cutaneous branch of median nerve
questions.answer: Palmar cutaneous branch of median nerve
questions.explanation: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve arises proximal to the flexor retinaculum and passes superficial to it, sparing palmar sensation.

questions.question: A motorcyclist suffers traction injury of the upper trunk (C5-C6) of the brachial plexus (Erb-Duchenne palsy). Which classic limb posture is produced?
options: Adducted, internally rotated arm with pronated forearm (Waiter's tip)
Claw hand with loss of hypothenar eminence
Wrist drop with inability to extend digits
Ape hand deformity with thenar atrophy
questions.answer: Adducted, internally rotated arm with pronated forearm (Waiter's tip)
questions.explanation: Loss of abductors (deltoid, supraspinatus) and lateral rotators produces adduction and internal rotation. Loss of biceps causes forearm pronation.

questions.question: Which tendon of the rotator cuff is most commonly involved in impingement syndrome and degenerative tears?
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon passes directly beneath the rigid coracoacromial arch in a critical hypovascular zone, making it most vulnerable to impingement.
